svg.aria-label: How to write ി: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing ി
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ി (malayalam), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table III 'How to Write Internal Vowel Symbols', p. xx: movement 1 for ി, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-030.jpg>. Source note on variation: Moag's Table III (p. xx) draws it as one movement to the right of the dash: from the curled tip over the top and down the stem. Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. Santhosh Thottingal's hand reference curves (gitlab.com/santhoshtr/hand, MIT, 2019), which keep several strokes where a glyph has them, record ി as one stroke from the upper left to the lower right. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker, but none of the 26 unique samples jumps between consecutive points the way a lift would; they most often start at the upper left (26 of 26) and end at the lower right (24 of 26). The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline of the sign on its own rather than to Moag's drawing.
